messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Age: 58 years
Gender: Male
Date of Admission: June 8, 2020
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Reason for Admission:
The patient was admitted on June 8, 2020, due to increased oxygen requirements following a COVID-19 diagnosis.

Hospital Course:
The patient received high flow nasal cannula therapy on admission. However, on hospital day 6, mechanical ventilation (MV) was initiated due to respiratory distress, hypoxemia, and hypercapnia. Despite MV, the patient's respiratory failure continued to worsen. Therefore, venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) was implemented on hospital day 11. Meropenem, levofloxacin, convalescent plasma therapy, and dexamethasone were administered during the treatment course.

Outcome:
The patient showed gradual improvement in lung compliance and chest radiography. Ultimately, VV-ECMO was discontinued on hospital day 38.

Follow-Up Care:
The patient will continue to receive follow-up care and monitoring as required for complete recovery.
Primary Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]Secondary Diagnoses: [diagnosis section withheld]
Co-Morbidities:
None

Procedures Performed:
MV and VV-ECMO were performed during hospitalization.

Medications Upon Discharge:
There were no medications prescribed at the time of discharge.

Recommendations:
The patient was advised to continue following a healthy lifestyle routine and receiving regular medical checkups.

Clinical Team:
- Attending Physician: [REDACTED]
- Nurse: [REDACTED]
- ECMO Specialist: [REDACTED]
- Respiratory Therapist: [REDACTED]
- Pharmacist: [REDACTED]
- Social Worker: [REDACTED]

Discharge Instructions:
The patient was advised to rest and follow a healthy routine as per routine health guidelines. The patient was informed of follow-up appointments and instructed to contact the hospital in case of any concerns or queries.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is COVID-19 with severe respiratory failure. The patient was admitted for increased oxygen requirements, and the course involved ventilation and ECMO for pneumonia and ARDS. In ICD-10-AM, COVID-19 is coded in chapter U as U07.1 (virus identified), with the manifestations coded as additional diagnoses. The principal diagnosis category is therefore U07.

CODE: U07
